method: Same AI, separate source-first pass after freezing. Began with the dated Groningen scheme and the LEX004B10 record and reconstructed credit totals, elective groups and prior study. Reconsidered literature, linguistics, rhetoric, film, and research contributions in the active UCR workbook and checked the resulting records against those sources. Worker A performed both passes.
findings: The English-taught Groningen BA English Language and Culture is 180 EC. The example follows September 2026 entrants, for whom the dated scheme records six first-year courses worth 10 EC each. Year two combines three compulsory 10 EC courses, one 10 EC IMPACT selection and four 5 EC electives. Year three has a 30 EC minor or free space, four different 5 EC electives, and the 10 EC Portfolio or BA Thesis. The required LEX004B10 is listed in semester two and gives a thematic individual portfolio or a thesis for some students. The older LEX003B10 is listed separately and uses legacy requirements. This example represents the shared interdisciplinary degree and keeps a balance of literature, linguistics, communication and global culture, while preparing for the linguistics final project.

The first semester introduces structure and social contexts in English Linguistics 1, Professional English 1 and Understanding English Literatures. The second includes medieval literature, Professional English 2 and mediated identities. Professional English 2 builds on the first course. In year two the compulsory first-semester courses cover cognition and language development, identities and ideologies, and Anglophone literary transformations. The IMPACT selection runs across semester two. Sociolinguistics Laboratory and Flux occupy group A, with World Literatures in English and Learning and Teaching English in group B. The Laboratory requires a positive first-year study recommendation and completed English Linguistics 1. The plan completes these and has 60 EC from year two, including three LET courses: the compulsory cognitive linguistics course, Laboratory and Learning and Teaching English. This clears the published LEX004B10 threshold of all 60 first-year EC plus 50 further EC including three linguistics courses before the final project. Professional English 3 is moved to Year 3 group B and follows completed Professional English 1. Language in Interaction and Strangers occupy group A, with Literary Theories and Professional English 3 in group B. Each group has two different electives. Future years use the dated scheme as the published planning example.

The closest option combines genre and close reading, world literature, life writing and literary theory with stylistics, psycholinguistics, rhetoric and contextual work in film and the American Century. Rhetoric in Action moves to the final spring after the introductory course and complements the documentary, historical and creative projects. The literature and media option adds film history, media archaeology, empire, Indigenous histories, gender and museum and art-history methods. Heritage and ancient democracy contribute contextual interpretation and contested citizenship, rather than English literary history. The language option builds from Brain & Behavior and rhetoric into psycholinguistics, language and style, philosophy of mind and later work on higher cognition, persuasion and research synthesis. Conflict and social theory are contextual contributions to public discourse and identity. Description-only Psycholinguistics gives direct acquisition and language-processing evidence, Perspectives on Literary Meaning supports critical theory, Writing Art’s Histories supports historiography and Communicating the Climate Crisis contributes analysis of public argument. The three alternatives exceed the pairwise course-difference floor. The alignment preserves the modern and medieval English literary sequences, conversation analysis, sociolinguistics, teaching English and the final project as distinct requirements. The poetry lab and psychology meta-analysis remain complementary courses, without claims of interactional linguistics or subject-specific thesis equivalence. The 15 EC optional UCR research element is comparison-only.
